newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius share index down in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius share index down in lower volume.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Mauritius share index (semdex) eased in lower volume on Friday, under the weight of falling stocks of the national carrier and leading conglomerate Ireland Blythe, brokers said.
Semdex was down 0.92 points to 321.40. Turnover was provisionally posted at 4.53 million rupees on 148,439 shares from 12.41 million rupees on 300,641 shares on Wednesday.
A 40 percent slump in interim profit for the half year to 30 June 1996 reported by conglomerate Ireland Blyth on Thursday resulted in its shares losing ground, brokers said.
Ireland Blyth lost 20 cents to 13 rupees on 4,890 shares.
"(Ireland Blyth) was more or less expected to report such type of interim results," a broker told Reuters.
"Its performance in 1995 was not brilliant either and with prevailing difficult conditions in the local commercial sector, the news did not break out as a big surprise," the broker said.
"This (performance by Ireland Blythe) somewhat limited the downward movement of its shares today (Friday)," he added.
Air Mauritius fell by 2.0 rupees to 51 on 3,110 shares as small investors were seen selling shares of the airline.
The fall of Air Mauritius and Ireland Blyth stocks offset rising shares of a few other listed companies with the net result the Semdex lost ground, bourse officials said.
Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 73 rupees on 13,012 shares and State Bank of Mauritius was stable at 8.40 rupees on 38,014 shares.
British American Insurance gained 20 cents to 7.50 rupees on 10,000 shares and Swan Insurance was 60 cents higher to 30.20 rupees on 500 shares.

Mauritius Breweries remained at 125 rupees on 14,647 shares. Brokers said foreign investor bought the breweries stocks owing to the high volume. Mauritius Chemical Fertilisers rose 30 cents to 10.50 rupees on 175 shares.
Investment-based Fincorp added 50 cents to 72 rupees on 1,158 shares and United Docks was unchanged at 40.80 rupees on 4,727 shares.
Conglomerate Rogers was stable at 94.50 rupees on 1,580 shares while commerce based Courts gained 20 cents to 3.80 rupees on 2,000 shares.
